verses.text: Some time later, during a Jewish festival, Jesus headed up to Jerusalem.
Near Jerusalem’s Sheep Gate was a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew, with five covered walkways.
A whole crowd of sick people was laid out there—blind, lame, and paralyzed—waiting for the water to move.
At certain times, an angel went down into the pool and stirred the water. The first person in after that was healed, whatever sickness they had.
One man there had been sick for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and clocked he’d been sick for a long time. He asked, “Do you want to get well?”
The man answered, “Sir, I have nobody to help me into the pool when the water moves. While I’m trying to get there, someone else slips in ahead of me.”
Jesus told him, “Get up, grab your mat, and walk.”
Right then, the man was healed. He picked up his mat and walked. And it was the Sabbath.
So the Jewish leaders said to the healed man, “It’s the Sabbath. The rules don’t let you carry that mat.”
He answered, “The man who healed me told me, ‘Grab your mat and walk.’”
They asked him, “Who told you, ‘Grab it and walk’?”
But the healed man didn’t know who it was. Jesus had slipped away into the crowd.
Later, Jesus found him in the temple and said, “Look, you’re well now. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”
The man went and told the Jewish leaders it was Jesus who had healed him.
That’s why the leaders came after Jesus and tried to kill him: he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
Jesus replied, “My Father is still working, and I’m working too.”
That only made them want to kill him more. He wasn’t just breaking the Sabbath; he called God his own Father and made himself equal with God.
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you straight: the Son can’t do anything on his own. He only does what he sees the Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does too.
The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. He’ll show him even bigger works, and you’ll be amazed.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, the Son gives life to whoever he chooses.
The Father doesn’t judge anyone; he has given all judgment to the Son,
so everyone will honor the Son just like they honor the Father. Whoever disrespects the Son disrespects the Father who sent him.”
“I’m telling you straight: whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life. They won’t be judged; they’ve crossed over from death into life. 🌅
I’m telling you straight: the time is coming—and it’s already here—when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice. Those who hear will live.
The Father has life in himself, and he gave the Son life in himself too.
He also gave the Son authority to judge, because he is the Son of Man.
Don’t be shocked by this. The time is coming when everyone in the tombs will hear his voice
and come out: those who did good will rise to life, and those who did evil will rise to face judgment.
I can do nothing on my own. I judge as I hear, and my judgment is right because I’m not chasing my own will, but the will of the Father who sent me.”
“If I testified about myself, my testimony wouldn’t stand.
Someone else speaks up about me, and I know his testimony about me is true.
You sent people to John, and he told the truth.
I don’t rely on human testimony, but I’m saying this so you can be saved.
John was a lamp, burning and shining bright, and for a while you were happy to enjoy his light.
But the proof I have tops John’s: the works the Father gave me to finish—the very works I’m doing—show that the Father sent me.
The Father who sent me has testified about me, but you’ve never heard his voice or seen his form.
His word isn’t living in you, because you don’t trust the one he sent.”
“You comb through the Scriptures because you think eternal life is in them. But they’re the ones pointing to me.
And still, you refuse to come to me to receive life.
I don’t take praise from people.
But I know you: God’s love isn’t in you.
I came in my Father’s name, and you won’t accept me. If someone comes in his own name, you’ll accept him.
How can you believe when you’re hyping each other up but don’t seek the praise that comes from the only God?”
“Don’t think I’m going to accuse you to the Father. Moses—the one you’ve put your hope in—is the one accusing you.
If you really believed Moses, you’d believe me, because he wrote about me.
But if you don’t believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”
